title: Introduce quantile-slice hedger and stochastic cutover circuit
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see transient tail regressions during small traffic bursts that cause binary rollback decisions in the canary orchestrator. Those rollbacks are noisy for low-risk regressions and make gradual rollouts brittle for multi-tenant workloads. This PR introduces two complementary controls: (1) a quantile-slice hedger that evaluates distributional drift across time-sliced quantiles and emits a graded instability score, and (2) a stochastic cutover circuit that converts high-frequency binary cutovers into probabilistic, smoothed attenuation actions (traffic attenuation / short-circuiting) to avoid synchronized rollbacks across cohorts.

Summary of changes: implemented a new hedger component in the perf-canary evaluator, wire-up to the canary orchestrator for soft attenuation actions, added end-to-end tests and synthetic scenarios, and added dashboards and runbook guidance. The approach focuses on reducing false-positive full rollbacks while still surfacing sustained regressions for human review.

Design highlights: 
- Quantile-slice hedger: splits recent request latency samples into N temporal slices (configurable, default 5) and computes target quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) per slice. The hedger computes inter-slice deltas and a weighted entropy score that downweights short-lived spikes and upweights persistent shifts. Output is a normalized instability score [0,1] and an ordinal severity (ok/warn/degrade).
- Stochastic cutover circuit: when instability enters warn/degrade, instead of immediate rollback we apply a probabilistic attenuation policy: a percentage of traffic is diverted to a fallback model or throttled for short randomized windows. The circuit uses a low-disruption schedule (Poisson-based jitter + exponential backoff on repeated hits) so multiple tenants or regions don't cut over synchronously.
- Integration: instability score is exposed to the canary orchestrator as part of the evaluation result. Orchestrator mapping now supports action types: none, attenuation, canary-pause, full-rollback. Default policy for warn => attenuation; degrade => attenuation + notify.

Testing & validation: 
- Unit tests for hedger scoring math and entropy weighting.
- Synthetic integration tests that replay production-ish traffic traces with injected transient and sustained regressions to verify attenuation triggers vs rollback triggers.
- End-to-end smoke tests to validate orchestration actions and that traffic is routed correctly under attenuation.
- CI flaky test re-run: one integration test failed on first run (timing-dependent), re-run passed. Full pipeline green on final commit.

Operational notes: 
- New config flags added (perf_canary.hedger.slice_count, perf_canary.hedger.quantiles, perf_canary.circuit.base_attenuation_pct). Defaults are conservative and backwards compatible.
- Added a new dashboard tab `Hedger / Cutover` showing per-cohort instability score, recent slice quantiles heatmap, and attenuation action history.
- Runbook updated with guidance: for persistent degrade (instability > 0.6 for 10m) teams should follow the existing rollback playbook. Soft attenuation is intended as a transient mitigation.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests (synthetic scenarios)
- [x] Dashboard and runbook updates
- [x] Feature flagged behind perf_canary.hedger.enabled (off in prod by default)

Risk / mitigation: 
- Risk: attenuation could mask real regressions. Mitigation: attenuation is accompanied by persistent telemetry and alerts; the hedger severity escalates to degrade for sustained issues.
- Risk: added compute overhead from quantile slicing. Mitigation: sampling rate and slice_count are configurable; hedger runs in a separate lightweight evaluation worker to avoid blocking the primary pipeline.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged once reviewers ran the integration harness in staging and CI was green.

Related work: references ENG-1947 for rollouts reliability story and ENG-1952 for attenuation policy spec.

Notes for reviewers: look for correctness in entropy weighting and the attenuation scheduling; pay attention to the test that re-ran in CI (integration/synthetic/cutover_schedule_test) and comment if the jitter constants need tuning.

review_comments: Samir Patel (2024-11-05): Nice concise design. One ask: please document why we choose Poisson jitter for attenuation windows vs uniform jitter. Also add a small benchmark for hedger CPU overhead.
Maya Chen (2024-11-06): replied: Poisson jitter chosen to reduce chance of simultaneous alignment across cohorts; added micro-benchmark (hedger_benchmark) and documented reasoning in hedger.md.
Olivia Hart (2024-11-08): requested change: make default slice_count configurable via env var and lower default to 5. Verified in staging with sample traces.
Maya Chen (2024-11-09): addressed and pushed change, updated tests and CI config.
release_notes: Adds quantile-slice hedger scoring and a stochastic cutover circuit to enable soft attenuation actions during transient regressions. Feature is feature-flagged off by default. Includes dashboards and runbook guidance.
